Proposition
[Centralizers in hyperbolic three-manifolds] 1. Proposition 5.4.4\group hyperbolic 3-manifoldsSource: thurston:page-0107, thurston:page-0108 If $a,b\in \pi _1M$ commute in a complete hyperbolic $3$--manifold, then either they lie in one infinite cyclic subgroup, or they lie with finite index in the peripheral group of a torus end.
Proof

\sketch Hyperbolic commuting elements share an axis and discreteness makes their translations cyclic. Otherwise they are parabolic; independent translation vectors generate a Euclidean lattice on a horosphere, and the small-displacement abelian subgroup produces the corresponding torus cusp.

□
